question.value: Are there spatially resolved radio jets/lobes (AGN feedback) in the Phoenix cluster BCG, and what is the origin of the radio emission near the center?

evidence.quote: Key information missing so far is whether or not there are radio jets/lobes, which are firm evidence of AGN feedback activities.

bands.value: ALMA Band 3, center 92 GHz (combined with ATCA 15 mm data)

evidence.quote: we combined ALMA Band 3 data of the Phoenix cluster (see (cite: kit20) for details). The center frequency is 92 GHz
the beam FWHM is $1.9\ensuremath{''} \times 1.6\ensuremath{''}$ (using $>30k\lambda$ baselines)

provided.value: Primary 15 mm (17 and 19 GHz) observations, 6A configuration, Project C3190

evidence.quote: Our observations were made with the ATCA in November 1 and 2 in 2017 (Project C3190, see Table [\[t01\]](#t01)).

provided.value: Archival soft X-ray data (ObsID 13401, 16135, 16545) for residual map

evidence.quote: we made an X-ray surface brightness residual map using *Chandra X-ray Observatory* archival data of the Phoenix cluster (ObsID: 13401, 16135, and 16545).
*Hubble Space Telescope* (*HST*) F814W (814 nm, I band, (cite: mcd15), the coordinate offset is not corrected)

method.value: Point-source fits with IMFIT; error-weighted least-squares power-law fit of four in-band images

evidence.quote: We evaluated flux densities of Sources C1 and W using the MIRIAD task IMFIT with the option OBJECT=POINT.

analysis_steps.goal: Combine ATCA 18 GHz with ALMA 92 GHz for spectra and astrometric cross-match

method.value: Spectral index from ATCA 18 GHz and ALMA 92 GHz; positions cross-matched

evidence.quote: The results of the spectral index measurement using ATCA 18 GHz and ALMA 92 GHz data are shown in figure [2](#f02).

used_for.value: ATCA data reduction, imaging, self-calibration, flux fitting

evidence.quote: Data reduction was performed with the MIRIAD software (cite: sau95) version 1.5

results_numeric.quantity: Source C1 flux density at 18 GHz

evidence.quote: We obtained the flux densities of 3.395 $\pm$ 0.132 mJy for Source C1
We obtain a flatter ($\alpha=-0.37$) spectrum for Source C1 compared to the in-band spectrum
We obtained the in-band spectral index of $\alpha=-0.50$ for the brightest Source C1.
for Source W, $\alpha= -0.58$ and $-0.62$ with and without the data at 19.5 GHz in the fit

findings_qualitative.value: Diffuse bipolar structures aligned with X-ray cavities are likely radio lobes; C3 and C4 are likely young jets

evidence.quote: They are likely radio jets/lobes, whose sizes are $\sim 10$–$20$ kpc and locations are aligned with X-ray cavities.

claims.hypothesis: Radio jets/lobes exist in the Phoenix BCG
claims.experiment: ATCA 15 mm imaging at sub-arcsec resolution, compared with Chandra residuals
claims.result: Bipolar diffuse structures C5, C6 aligned with X-ray cavities
claims.finding: They are radio lobes with ages ~10 Myr

evidence.quote: both the Northern and Southern structures are aligned with X-ray negative regions (i.e. cavities).
